as_told.title: Donald Menzel destroys a third of the Harvard plates

plain: In the 1950s, a Harvard astronomer named Donald Menzel is said to have been caught destroying old photographic plates, the glass plates on which observatories recorded the night sky. The witness, as these tellers describe her, was Dorrit Hoffleit, a respected Harvard astronomer who worked under him and wrote about it in her memoirs. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, who studies old sky images, tells it most fully. She says Menzel helped the US Air Force explain away the 1952 Washington sightings and then, two or three months later, became director of the Harvard Observatory and destroyed a third of its photographic plates. Jesse Michels repeats the story several times, calling Hoffleit "very reputable" and pointing to her biography as the place where she records it. Why it matters to them: if those plates held images of strange objects in the sky, a record that could have been studied was lost.
